channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Samara Martins declara R$ 33 mil em bens ao TSE
item.description: Samara Martins, the UP party's presidential candidate, declared R$33,000 in assets to the TSE, an 880% increase from the R$3,364.55 she reported in 2022 when running for vice-president. Her running mate, Raquel Brício, reiterated she has no assets to declare, as she did in the 2020–2024 elections. The filings were made public by the TSE within the final deadline for candidate registration.

item.title: Corrida ao Senado no PR tem Deltan, Curi e Gleisi na frente; petista lidera rejeição
item.description: In Paraná, former deputy Deltan Dallagnol (Novo), state deputy Alexandre Curi (Republicanos), and federal deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT) lead voting intentions for the Federal Senate in 2026. Dallagnol is the best-positioned candidate, while Hoffmann tops the rejection index among contenders. The race is polarized between center-right and left-wing figures, with strong focus on anti-corruption and public management themes.

item.title: Lula tem 60% contra 35% de Flávio em 2º turno em PE, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll released on August 17, 2026, shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) 60% to 35% in a hypothetical second-round scenario in Pernambuco. In the first-round scenario, Lula holds 58% support versus Flávio’s 24%, with other candidates polling below 5%. The Lula government enjoys 61% approval in the state, while 53% of respondents say they would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Nexus: Lula e Flávio iniciam campanha com 3 pontos de diferença no 2º turno
item.description: Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) begin the 2026 presidential election campaign for the runoff with just a three-point gap, according to the BTG/Nexus poll. Lula holds 47% of voting intentions, while Flávio has 44%, with blank and null votes remaining stable. The narrow margin signals a highly competitive race from the outset.

item.title: Lula tem 47% contra 44% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz Nexus
item.description: A Nexus poll released on August 17, 2026, shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) by 47% to 44% in a hypothetical 2026 presidential election runoff, with the two candidates technically tied within the 2-point margin of error. The survey, conducted August 14–16 among 2,003 Brazilian voters and registered with the TSE as BR-03317/2026, also found Flávio rejected by 50% of respondents and Lula by 48%, while Lula’s government approval stands at 47% and disapproval at 48%.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro mantêm empate técnico no 2º turno, com 47% a 44%
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll released on Monday (17) shows that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) remain in a technical tie in the 2026 runoff, with 47% and 44% of voting intentions, respectively. The three-point difference falls within the margin of error, indicating no statistically significant advantage for either candidate.

item.title: Lula visita navio-sonda da Petrobras na Margem Equatorial
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visits Petrobras' drilling vessel in the Equatorial Margin, following the state oil company's announcement of hydrocarbon presence in the area. Petrobras disclosed the finding on Friday, and Lula is expected to comment on the matter at Oiopoque Airport in Amapá on Monday. The visit underscores the government's focus on natural resource exploration in the Amazon region.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Para 42%, governo Lula é ruim ou péssimo; 34% consideram ótimo ou bom e 23% regular
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows that 42% of voters rate Lula's government as bad or terrible, down from 44% in the August 10 survey — a change within the margin of error. Meanwhile, 34% consider the government good or excellent, unchanged from the previous poll, and 23% rate it as regular.

item.title: Lula elogia trato com Trump, mas avisa: não se meta na eleição
item.description: Lula leads the 2026 presidential race in the first round with 38% versus 31% for Flávio Bolsonaro, but the runoff shows a technical tie with only a 3-point gap. Both candidates face high rejection rates (52% for Lula, 54% for Flávio), while 51% of voters remain undecided in spontaneous responses. Lula praised Trump’s treatment in their talks but warned against any U.S. interference in Brazil’s electoral process, demanding respect for national sovereignty.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: presidente Lula é aprovado por 47%; 48% o desaprovam
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows President Lula with 47% approval and 48% disapproval, a technical tie within the margin of error. In the first round of the 2026 election, Lula leads with 41% voting intention, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (36%) and Ronaldo Caiado (5%). In the second round, Lula is technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro (47% each) and also with Caiado.

item.title: Lula tem 47% e Flávio 44 % em cenário de 2º turno, mostra pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula at 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 44% in a hypothetical runoff, technically tied within the 2-point margin of error. The result has remained stable since August 10, with Lula also in a technical tie against Ronaldo Caiado (46% vs 42%) and Romeu Zema (46% vs 41%), while holding a clear lead over Renan Santos (47% vs 37%). Blank, null, and undecided voters range from 8% to 14% depending on the scenario.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula seguem como mais rejeitados, com 50 % e 48%, respectivamente
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) remain the most rejected presidential candidates in Brazil, with 50% and 48% rejection rates, respectively, according to the BTG/Nexus poll. Their rejection levels are technically tied, reflecting deep polarization in the 2026 electoral landscape.

item.title: No 1º turno, Lula lidera com 41% e Flávio Bolsonaro tem 36%, aponta pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: Lula leads the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election with 41% of voting intentions, according to the BTG/Nexus poll. Flávio Bolsonaro follows in second place with 36%.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula tem 47% e Flávio 44 % no 2º turno, seguem empatados tecnicamente
item.description: Lula leads Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff with 47% to 44%, according to the BTG/Nexus poll, but the two remain technically tied within the margin of error. The three-point lead is not statistically significant.

item.title: Lula mantém vantagem numérica sobre Flávio, mas empate técnico persiste, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: Lula maintains a numerical lead over Flávio Bolsonaro, but a technical tie persists in a potential runoff, according to the BTG/Nexus poll. The president remains ahead of the Rio de Janeiro senator, though the difference falls within the margin of error.

item.title: Funcionária de Trump chama regra eleitoral do Brasil de “censura”
item.description: U.S. Deputy Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy Sarah B. Rogers criticized Brazil’s electoral rule as 'censorship,' claiming it restricts the recommendation of candidate profiles and posts on social media. The rule, based on TSE Resolution 23.610 of 2019, requires platforms like X to exclude from algorithmic recommendations accounts notified to the Electoral Justice for the 2026 elections. X implemented the 'Brazil2026ElectionFilter' to comply, reducing the visibility of such accounts while keeping their content accessible on their direct pages.

item.title: EUA consideram novas sanções contra Alexandre de Moraes, diz jornal britânico
item.description: The Financial Times reports that the U.S. government is considering new sanctions against Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes over recent rulings sparking press freedom debates. Moraes was previously sanctioned in 2023 under the Magnitsky Act for alleged human rights abuses but was removed from the list in December following a diplomatic thaw between Trump and Lula. Reimposing sanctions could worsen U.S.-Brazil tensions, affecting trade and casting a shadow over the 2026 elections.

item.title: Saiba o que candidatos ao Planalto farão nesta 2ª feira
item.description: Presidential candidates are following varied schedules this Monday (Aug. 17, 2026), involving regional trips, economic events, and political meetings. Lula travels to Amapá to visit a Petrobras platform on the Equatorial Margin; Bolsonaro participates in a motorcycle rally in Juiz de Fora; Caiado, Zema, and Renan Santos attend the 27th Annual Santander Conference in São Paulo, alongside additional engagements.

item.title: Campanha de Lula planeja reunir 5 mil mulheres em encontro
item.description: President Lula's re-election campaign plans to gather approximately 5,000 women for a national meeting in Belo Horizonte on August 29 at the Serraria Souza Pinto cultural center. The event, titled 'National Meeting Women with Lula,' will focus on combating violence against women and femicide, featuring First Lady Janja and supporting candidates such as Benedita da Silva and Manuela d’Ávila. Additional topics include wage equality, women's health, political participation, and digital violence prevention.

item.title: Governo Lula: leia a agenda de ministros do governo nesta 2ª feira
item.description: On Monday, August 17, 2026, ten ministers from President Lula's government held public agendas in Brasília, São Paulo, Simões Filho (BA), and Porto Alegre (RS), focusing on economy, health, science and technology, ports and airports, and public advocacy. Activities included participation in banking conferences, opening of a tropical medicine congress, signing of scientific cooperation protocols, naval keel-laying ceremonies, and a public law forum. The schedules of 32 out of 38 ministers were not officially disclosed at the time of publication.

item.title: Saiba quais pesquisas eleitorais podem sair nesta 2ª feira
item.description: Electoral polls registered with the TSE are cleared for publication this Monday (Aug 17, 2026), covering national scenarios and the states of Pernambuco, Paraná, Amazonas, and the municipality of Macaé (RJ). Poder360 highlights its Poll Aggregator, available to Drive subscribers, which compiles thousands of polls since 2000 with validated methodology from the Electoral Justice. Subscribers can access full data via email or platform; non-subscribers can explore subscription plans.

item.title: Agenda de Lula: leia os compromissos do presidente 2ª feira
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva carries out an official agenda in Amapá on Monday, August 17, 2026, visiting Petrobras operations in the Foz do Amazonas Basin, focusing on the survey vessel in block FZA-M-59. Following the technical visit, he gives a press interview in Oiapoque and returns to Brasília by the end of the day.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pede autógrafo a Neymar antes de derrota do Vasco para o Santos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a 2026 presidential candidate, held a rally in Copacabana and attended the Vasco vs. Santos match, where he requested an autograph from Neymar. He was accompanied by Douglas Ruas, Rio gubernatorial candidate, and met with Vasco president Pedrinho. Vasco lost 3-0.

item.title: Sergio Moro lidera disputa pelo governo do Paraná em 1º turno
item.description: Sergio Moro (PL-PR) leads the race for governor of Paraná with 46.1% of voting intentions in the first round, according to a Paraná Pesquisa survey released on August 17, 2026. Requião Filho (PDT-PR) is second with 23.4%, followed by Sandro Alex (PSD-PR) at 16.5%. The survey interviewed 1,520 people across 65 municipalities between August 13–16, 2026, with a 2.6-point margin of error and TSE registration PR-09048/2026.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula e Flávio estabilizam com empate técnico no 2º turno
item.description: President Lula (PT) maintains a five-point percentage lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in voting intentions for the first round of the 2026 presidential election, according to the BTG/Nexus poll released on August 17. The advantage remains unchanged from the previous survey on August 10, indicating stability in the race. While the title references a technical tie in the runoff, the data shows Lula leading in the first round.

item.title: Campanha no Brasil começa em clima de tensão com EUA, comparações entre governos e até chamado divino
item.description: The Brazilian electoral campaign has officially opened amid rising tensions, characterized by ideological clashes between left and right, strain in trade and diplomatic relations with the United States, and even religious invocations by some candidates. The environment is seen as one of the most challenging for both political spectrums, with emphasis on government comparisons and narratives of national crisis.

item.title: Lula ou Flávio Bolsonaro: Nova pesquisa mostra quem tem a maior rejeição na largada da campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) begins the campaign with a 50% rejection rate, slightly higher than Lula’s (PT) 48%, according to the BTG/Nexus poll, within the two-point margin of error. Lula leads in first-round voting intention at 41% versus Flávio’s 36%, and in a hypothetical runoff holds 47% to Flávio’s 44% — also a technical tie. Polarization is pronounced, with 29% of voters identified as staunch Bolsonarists and 25% as staunch Lulists, showing strong loyalty within each base.

item.title: Lula quer fugir do debate da Band
item.description: President Lula has decided not to participate in the TV Band debate scheduled for next Sunday, citing unequal conditions among candidates. The decision was confirmed by Folha de S. Paulo and O Antagonista following a meeting with his campaign team. Lula aims to avoid the event, arguing that the debate conditions are not fair or equitable.

item.title: Campanha começa com Lula seguido de perto por adversários no segundo turno, diz BTG Nexus
item.description: Lula is technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro (47% to 44%) and Ronaldo Caiado (45% to 42%) in a potential runoff, according to the BTG Nexus poll. In the first-round simulation, Lula leads with 41% of voting intentions, followed by the PL senator at 36%. Rejection rates for Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are nearly identical at 48% and 50%, respectively.

item.title: BTG: Lula lidera 1º turno, mas segue empatado com Flávio e Caiado no 2º
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula leading in the first round with 41% voting intentions, ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (36%) and Ronaldo Caiado (5%), with the difference outside the margin of error. In the second round, Lula is technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro (47% vs 44%) and Ronaldo Caiado (45% vs 42%), maintaining stability compared to the previous round. Other tested scenarios (Lula vs Romeu Zema and Lula vs Renan Santos) also show the petista ahead.

item.title: Custo para governo funcionar soma R$ 33,3 bilhões
item.description: Administrative spending by the Brazilian federal government reached R$ 33.3 billion in the first half of 2026, a 10.7% increase from the same period in 2025, according to the National Treasury. This marks the highest first-semester spending since 2014, with support services accounting for R$ 16.7 billion, followed by IT, fuels, and property leases. The figure covers only operational maintenance costs, excluding investments.

item.title: Federação do Pará pede que governo decrete emergência para viabilizar dragagem do rio Tapajós vetada por Lula
item.description: The Federation of Industries of the State of Pará (Fiepa) urged Governor Hana Ghassan to declare a state of emergency due to risks of falling river levels and potential disruption of navigation on the Tapajós River, a measure previously vetoed by President Lula.

item.title: 'Neutralidade' do centrão serve a Lula em palanques eleitorais estratégicos
item.description: The 2026 presidential campaign officially begins with the 'centrão' adopting a stance of neutrality that, in practice, serves Lula's re-election bid in strategic electoral strongholds. This assessment is shared by third-way strategists, who view the centrão as a key factor in balancing political forces without undermining support for the current president.

item.title: Candidato 'médio' de 2026 é homem, branco, hétero e empresário
item.description: The most common profile of candidates in the 2026 Brazilian elections is a white, heterosexual, male businessman around 49.5 years old. Although the content mentions 'black', the title and overall context suggest the dominant profile is white, indicating a possible inconsistency or error in the original text. This pattern reflects the persistence of racial, gender, and class inequalities in political representation.

item.title: Flávio aposta em local da facada em Bolsonaro para alavancar palanque em MG
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL presidential candidate, launched his campaign in Copacabana and is now traveling to Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais, where his father, Jair Bolsonaro, was stabbed in 2018. The symbolic location aims to mobilize emotional and political support tied to the assassination attempt.

item.title: Foto de Renan com Lula e pressão de Lira explicam reviravolta de JHC em AL
item.description: Former Maceió mayor João Henrique Caldas (JHC, PSDB) announced his candidacy for governor of Alagoas, withdrawing from the Senate race after a week of political turmoil. His decision was influenced by a photo of Renan Calheiros with Lula and pressure from Chamber President Arthur Lira, prompting him to shift his electoral strategy.

item.title: Gasto com funcionalismo atinge R$ 214,4 bilhões no 1º semestre
item.description: Union spending on personnel and social charges reached R$ 214.4 billion in the first half of 2026, representing a real increase of 10.6% compared to 2025. Despite the rise in total spending, the number of active federal civil servants decreased by 0.74% over 12 months, from 573,485 to 569,230. Excluding court judgments and precatórios, personnel spending was R$ 203.7 billion, with a real increase of 5.8%.

item.title: Esperar o quê?
item.description: According to a Metrópoles poll of 1,058 readers, 81.5% expect Lula to win the officially launched presidential campaign, while 8.7% favor Flávio and 9.8% anticipate a surprise. The piece also includes related articles and cartoons, highlighting Lula’s early lead in the race.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro teve 15% do público que o pai levou a Copacabana de quatro anos atrás
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro held an event at Copacabana beach to launch his 2026 presidential campaign, attempting to emulate his father Jair Bolsonaro’s past success at the same location. The article reports that the crowd size was only 15% of what Jair Bolsonaro had drawn in similar events four years earlier. Access to the full story requires a subscription and user registration.

item.title: Flávio cogitou Michelle na vice após desandar negociação com Tereza Cristina e Daniella Marques
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign considered Michelle Bolsonaro as a vice-presidential candidate after negotiations with the PP-União Brasil federation and Republicans failed, leading both to declare neutrality. The idea was rejected by allies as 'too much Bolsonaro on a ticket,' and other female PL figures were deemed 'too far right.' Flávio faces 50% rejection among women voters, per Datafolha, intensifying the need for a vice-presidential pick that could improve his appeal to female electorate.

item.title: Mulher de Haddad deixa governo para atuar na campanha de Lula em SP
item.description: Ana Estela Haddad, wife of Finance Minister Fernando Haddad, resigned as head of the Ministry of Health's Digital Information and Health Secretariat to join the coordination of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election campaign in São Paulo. She will focus on engaging universities, public officials, and opinion-forming sectors, following an invitation from lawyer Marco Aurélio de Carvalho of the Prerrogativas group, negotiated with Health Minister Alexandre Padilha.

item.title: As ameaças que rondam a retomada de julgamento sobre eleição para governador-tampão no Rio
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court will resume judgment on the format of the election for Rio de Janeiro’s interim governor mandate on the 19th, but a new request for view is expected after the process was returned by Flávio Dino. Ministers anticipate the interruption may come from Alexandre de Moraes or Gilmar Mendes, potentially delaying the decision by up to 90 days and pushing the outcome beyond the October regular elections.

item.title: Valdemar elege um culpado por público reduzido em ato de Flávio no Rio
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the PL, attributed the low turnout at Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign launch in Copacabana to cloudy weather, downplaying the weak attendance. The event drew between 7,800 and 9,900 people, according to estimates from USP's Monitor do Debate Político and More in Common, falling short of allies' expectations. Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly said no one matches his father, Jair Bolsonaro, in mobilization capacity.

item.title: Se Pablo Marçal está inelegível por 8 anos, por que foi anunciado como candidato à Presidência?
item.description: Pablo Marçal was announced as a presidential candidate by PRTB despite being ineligible until 2032 due to a judicial decision, as his candidacy was filed on the deadline (August 15) following an injunction that allowed his retroactive party affiliation. Experts state that while ineligibility is only confirmed by the TSE upon reviewing the candidacy registration, the likely outcome is negative, with his chances of running considered zero.

item.title: Motta próximo a Lula não evita distanciamento nacional do Republicanos
item.description: Hugo Motta, Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies and a member of the Republicans party, announced his support for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election, contradicting his party’s national decision to remain neutral in the 2026 presidential race. Although the party allowed state-level alliances, most regional leaders favor Flávio Bolsonaro, with only one member voting for a formal Lula alliance at the national convention. Motta justified his stance as aligned with Paraíba’s interests and what he believes is 'best for the country,' despite having recorded a video supporting a rival of his local Senate ally.

item.title: Centrão se reaproxima de Lula, e Alcolumbre, Motta e Lira evitam Flávio durante eleição
item.description: President Lula has successfully reapproached key Centrão leaders, including Hugo Motta and Davi Alcolumbre, who are now avoiding support for Flávio Bolsonaro. This shift stems from the perception that Lula leads in polls and has a stronger chance of winning in 2026, alongside agreements to maintain congressional control in 2027. The scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro, exposed by The Intercept, further distanced PP and União Brasil bosses, who adopted neutrality in crucial states like Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais.

item.title: Lula sai na frente do primeiro dia da campanha para presidente
item.description: Lula leads the 2026 presidential campaign with a significant first-round advantage over all opponents, including Flávio Bolsonaro, despite a technical tie in the second round. On the first official day of campaigning, his rally in São Bernardo do Campo showed greater mobilization and emotional resonance than Flávio’s event in Copacabana, reinforcing his message of social inclusion and criticism of the previous administration. The left is united behind Lula, while the right is fragmented, with only the PL backing Flávio and the Centrão split regionally.

item.title: Lula antecipa herança para filhos, e patrimônio cai 35%
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's asset declaration submitted to the Electoral Court in 2024 shows a 35.6% reduction in his patrimony, decreasing from R$7.4 million in 2022 to R$4.8 million. Allies attribute the drop to the early distribution of inheritance to his children. The report is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Exército reduz em mais de 50% a presença de militares na disputa eleitoral de 2026
item.description: The Brazilian Army will have only 50 military personnel running for elected office in the 2026 elections — five on active duty and 45 from the reserve — marking the lowest participation in history. This represents a reduction of over 50% compared to previous elections, signaling a shift in the Armed Forces’ traditional involvement in the electoral process. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Amiga de Lulinha comprou solitários e colar de diamantes para braço-direito de Lula, diz PF
item.description: The Federal Police intercepted dialogues between lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger and Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, former close aide to President Lula, revealing she gifted him a diamond solitaire pair and a diamond necklace in April 2024. The messages, alongside personal bill payments and a R$ 249,000 loan, suggest a scheme to gain influence in Lula’s inner circle through influence peddling. Roberta, a friend of Lulinha, is already under investigation for R$ 1.5 million in transfers from lobbyist Careca do INSS, linked to Operation Sem Desconto.
